generation.conditions: Room temperature, standard atmospheric conditions, and uniform strain application during tensile testing.

generation.mechanism: FCC materials have more slip systems available for dislocation movement, allowing for greater plastic deformation before fracture.
generation.predicted_outcome: FCC materials will demonstrate significantly higher ductility (greater elongation before fracture) compared to BCC materials.
generation.baseline: Ductility measurements of standard FCC and BCC materials under identical testing conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to comparing ductility between FCC and BCC materials under tensile loading conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The exact degree of ductility difference between FCC and BCC materials is uncertain and may vary based on specific alloy compositions and processing histories.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If FCC materials do not exhibit higher ductility than BCC materials under identical conditions, the hypothesis is falsified.
